answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.

answerNotes.BARK: Bark is a tree's protective outer covering. Its color and texture can help distinguish one kind of tree from another.
answerNotes.SHED: A shed is a small storage building. In a garden scene, it may hold tools and supplies rather than livestock.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.

answerNotes.WOOL: Wool comes from sheep. It can be spun into yarn and then knitted or woven into warm fabric.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.

answerNotes.SHELL: Shell means a hard outer covering. The same everyday word can describe the outside of an egg, nut, or crab.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.

answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
